VSCode-UTCS 1.135.3 connects the Extensions view to Open VSX and adds one-click SSH to the UTCS lab machines. It also fixes C/C++ autocomplete and pulls in upstream bug and security fixes through VS Code 1.140.

## What's new

- **Extensions work again.**
  - The Extensions view now uses the [Open VSX](https://open-vsx.org) marketplace.
  - AI extensions such as Claude and Codex, language packs and themes install from it directly.
  - Signature verification is off by default, because Open VSX extensions are not signed the way Microsoft's marketplace signs them. You can turn it back on with `extensions.verifySignature`.
- **SSH to the UTCS lab machines.**
  - Click the remote indicator in the bottom-left corner and choose **Connect to UTCS Lab Machine...**.
  - The list holds every machine from the [lab status page](https://apps.cs.utexas.edu/unixlabstatus/), with live load and user counts when the page is reachable.
  - **Least busy machine** picks one for you. You enter your CS username once, and it's remembered.
  - [Open Remote - SSH](https://github.com/jeanp413/open-remote-ssh) is now built in. Every release publishes the Linux server it installs on the remote machine.
- **C/C++ autocomplete only suggests what you include.**
  - Word suggestions used to come from every open C/C++ file. They now come from the current file and the open headers it `#include`s.
  - `editor.wordBasedSuggestionsIncludeDepth` sets how deep nested includes are followed. The default is 1 (direct includes only); 0 means the current file only.
- **First-run setup fixed.**
  - The setup dialog no longer offers a GitHub Copilot sign-in, and its button reads **Get Started**.
  - Its theme picker offers *VSCode-UTCS Dark* and *Light*, with Dark preselected.
- **No empty chat panel.**
  - New windows no longer open a Chat view whose buttons did nothing. It appears once an extension provides a chat participant.
  - The secondary side bar starts hidden.

## Security fixes from upstream

- Importing a chat session clears its Markdown trust and normalizes its URIs.
- DOMPurify is updated to 3.4.16 in the workbench and to 3.4.15 in the Markdown extension.

## Bug fixes from upstream (through 1.140)

- Remote connections reconnect after the computer wakes from sleep, instead of giving up because the grace time ran out while it was asleep.
- The mouse cursor no longer disappears after a native dialog opens.
- Closing a window that had a dock or taskbar badge no longer touches the destroyed window.
- More than 25 memory leaks fixed, including in:
  - terminal replay and scrollbars
  - semantic tokens, the search editor and custom editors
  - webview resource loading
  - SCM commands and chat participants
  - extension host telemetry
  - auxiliary windows, the editor view and the accessible view
- Editor:
  - Snippet whitespace in code actions is preserved.
  - Stale multi-diff document loads are ignored.
  - Font measurements survive short sessions.
- Custom editors that failed to open can be opened again.
- Git diffs wait for the repository to load.
- IME input in quick action searches resumes correctly.
- Portable mode on Windows uses its own taskbar identity.

## Installing

| Platform | File |
| --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | `VSCode-UTCS-*-win32-x64-user-setup.exe` |
| Linux x64 / arm64 | `VSCode-UTCS-*-linux-x86_64.AppImage` / `-linux-aarch64.AppImage` (`chmod +x`, then run it) |
| macOS Apple silicon / Intel | `VSCode-UTCS-*-darwin-arm64.dmg` / `-darwin-x64.dmg` |

The `vscode-utcs-reh-linux-*.tar.gz` files are the SSH remote servers. Open Remote - SSH downloads them by itself, so you don't need to install them.

The macOS app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. After dragging it to Applications, open it once with right-click → **Open**. If you instead see a message that it is "damaged", run:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VSCode-UTCS.app
```
